questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Consider the points $A(4\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 3\hat{k})$, $B(2\hat{j})$ and $C(-4\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 3\hat{k})$. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Position vectors of the points are given as $\vec{A} = 4\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$, $\vec{B} = 2\hat{j}$, and $\vec{C} = -4\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$.

The vectors $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{BC}$ are calculated as follows:

$\overrightarrow{AB} = \vec{B} - \vec{A} = (0 - 4)\hat{i} + (2 - 1)\hat{j} + (0 - 3)\hat{k} = -4\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$

$\overrightarrow{BC} = \vec{C} - \vec{B} = (-4 - 0)\hat{i} + (3 - 2)\hat{j} + (-3 - 0)\hat{k} = -4\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$

Since $\overrightarrow{AB} = \overrightarrow{BC}$, the vectors are parallel and share the common point $B$.

Therefore, the points $A$, $B$, and $C$ are collinear.

Answer: $A$, $B$ and $C$ are collinear.
